function: Jointly designs device transmit weights and server receive beamforming per round for over-the-air analog gradient aggregation, minimizing device transmit power subject to FL convergence conditions (pp. 3-4)
system: Single-antenna devices (M=10), server with N=16 antennas, uplink analog over-the-air aggregation of FedSGD gradients, 100 kHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 4, 10)
method: FedSGD (supervised) trains logistic regression on MNIST and ResNet14 on CIFAR-10 over the air; beamformer is alternating optimization with convex QP subproblems, not learned (pp. 4, 6-7, 10-12)
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. fading h~CN(0,I/PL) with COST Hata path loss, devices 10-100 m; MNIST and CIFAR-10 split evenly over devices; no standard channel model or measurements (pp. 10-12)
test_conditions: Fixed M=10, N=16; power limit swept 15-27 dBm, CSI error 0-0.2, 20 channel realizations; FL tested on dataset test split until 85% (MNIST) or 70% (CIFAR-10) accuracy (pp. 10-13)
baselines: Non-learned designs: MMSE (MSE bound), GSDS [25] (earlier published aggregation design, same authors), Bounded MSE (author-defined, after [4], [10], [12]); no learned beamformer baseline (p. 10)
metrics: Time-averaged total device transmit power (dBm), epochs to reach target test accuracy (85% MNIST, 70% CIFAR-10), AO convergence over iterations (pp. 10-13)
complexity: Per-round complexity O((M+N)^3) for the full algorithm, O(M^3) for the transmit-weight QP, O((M+N)^3) for the receive QP; independent of model size D (p. 8)
openness: Simulation code at https://github.com/faezemoradik/Power-Efficient-Over-the-Air-FL.git (footnote, p. 10); MNIST and CIFAR-10 are public datasets
q1_support: p. 10: "The path loss follows the COST Hata model [42], i.e.," with i.i.d. fading drawn as CN(0, I/PL); a custom simulator with only a Hata path loss, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "We consider M = 10 devices and N = 16 antennas" in every experiment; pp. 11-13 only sweep the power limit and the CSI error, and each dataset and model is trained separately.
q3_support: p. 10: "Greedy Spatial Device Selection (GSDS): [25]" is an earlier published aggregation design and "Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE)" a classical one; both are compared on total transmit power at equal epochs (Figs. 4, 6, 8, pp. 12-13).
q4_support: p. 8: "overall computational complexity of our proposed algorithm" with the initialization is O((M+N)^3) per round, independent of the model size D.
q5_support: p. 10: "The simulation codes are available online at" https://github.com/faezemoradik/Power-Efficient-Over-the-Air-FL.git (footnote 1).
notes: Passes no_learning only through the over-the-air FL rule: the beamformer is classical alternating optimization with QP subproblems and the learned element is the FL model (p. 4). Area 7: the problem is the over-the-air aggregation design with a 16-antenna server. q1 is 0: only the COST Hata path loss is used (not COST 2100). q3 rests on GSDS [25] (earlier design, same authors) and MMSE; MMSE and Bounded MSE are defined by the authors.
